note: The known attack classes, one taxonomy per language, each class the name of a test this repo must carry. /fluxpoint:init copies this file to .fluxpoint-attacks.json; spec-guard.py --check is then red for every class with neither a test of that name nor a waiver in its own taxonomy carrying a reason of at least 20 characters. A waiver is scoped to the taxonomy it sits in, so excusing a class on one side of the chain leaves the same id on the other side still owed. A taxonomy whose language the repo does not carry gates nothing, so a validator-only repo answers for the eUTxO classes alone and a builder-only repo for the off-chain ones alone. A language the repo does carry with no taxonomy here is the opposite case, and is named NO TAXONOMY with the classes this template holds for it: a note, or a failure once the manifest sets "requireAllLanguages": true. To gate only some halves on purpose, list them in "languages", for example ["typescript"]; a tracked language left out of that list is printed as excluded by declaration and never fails, and a taxonomy the manifest carries still gates whether or not the list names it. The single-taxonomy shape that shipped in 1.38.0, with language, classes and waived at the top level, is still read as one taxonomy.

taxonomies.note: The known eUTxO validator attack classes, each the name of a property test this repo must carry over aiken/fuzz. The test names are spec-guard obligation ids, so once written they are hashed and may not quietly weaken.

classes.property: One output cannot pay for two script inputs at once: for any transaction spending two inputs locked by this validator, the validator rejects it unless each input is matched by its own output. Count the paying outputs or the validating tokens across ALL script inputs, never only the one being validated.
classes.fuzz: a context with two inputs at this script's address and one output that would satisfy either alone

classes.property: An output that continues the contract goes to this script's address with the expected inline datum: the validator rejects any transaction whose continuing output is at another address, carries a foreign or missing datum, or names a datum hash the transaction does not resolve.
classes.fuzz: continuing outputs with a random address, a random datum, and a datum-by-hash the transaction does not carry

classes.property: A policy that mints one named token cannot be used to mint another: for any mint under this policy id with a token name or quantity other than the one expected, the policy rejects it. Check the whole value under the policy id, never only the presence of the expected token.
classes.fuzz: mint fields under the policy carrying extra token names and quantities beside the expected one

classes.property: Validation cost does not grow with attacker-supplied size: for values, datums or lists larger than the bound the contract documents, the validator rejects rather than iterating. A script that runs out of budget on a crafted input locks the funds it guards.
classes.fuzz: values with many token names and lists at and beyond the documented bound

classes.property: Address checks compare the full address, not only the payment credential: for any continuing output whose payment credential matches but whose staking credential was replaced, the validator rejects it.
classes.fuzz: outputs with the right payment credential and a random or absent stake credential

classes.property: Inputs this validator reads are its own: for any spent or reference input at another script's address carrying a datum this validator would accept, the validator rejects the transaction or restricts what that input may prove.
classes.fuzz: inputs at random script addresses carrying well-formed datums of the expected type

classes.property: Time-dependent logic requires a bounded validity range: for any transaction with an unbounded lower or upper validity bound where the contract reasons about time, the validator rejects it.
classes.fuzz: validity ranges with NegativeInfinity or PositiveInfinity bounds

classes.property: A spend that expects a mint or burn checks the exact policy, name and quantity: for any transaction that mints extra tokens under other policies, or a different quantity under the expected one, the validator rejects it.
classes.fuzz: mint fields with extra policies and with the expected policy at the wrong quantity

taxonomies.note: The known off-chain transaction builder attack classes. An agent calls the builder, the API and the indexer; the validator only ever sees what the builder produced, so a builder that can be talked into an out-of-spec transaction is the shorter path to the funds a correct validator guards. A class counts as specified when a tracked TypeScript test file (*.test.ts, *.spec.ts, or any .ts under test/, tests/ or __tests__/) names it in a test title or declares a function or const of that name. A match in a file that imports fast-check is a property over a generator; a match in a file without it is noted as an example.

classes.property: Change returns to an address the wallet controls: for any build request carrying a caller-supplied change address, the builder rejects the request or replaces the address with one whose payment credential the signing key derives. Compare the whole address, staking part included, against the set the wallet owns.
classes.fuzz: build requests whose change address is a random bech32 address, the wallet's own address with a foreign staking part, a script address, and an address from the other network id

classes.property: A datum survives encode then decode unchanged: for any datum this builder constructs, decoding its CBOR yields a value equal to the one encoded, and hashing the round-tripped bytes yields the datum hash the transaction carries. A datum that fails this is read by the validator as a different value than the builder wrote.
classes.fuzz: datums across the full field ranges: empty and maximal bytestrings, zero, negative and word64-sized integers, nested constructors at and past the depth the schema allows, maps with duplicate and unsorted keys, and every constructor index the type declares

classes.property: Every fee, min-ADA and execution-unit figure comes from protocol parameters fetched for the epoch the transaction is submitted in: for a cached parameter set older than the current epoch boundary, the builder refetches or refuses to build. A transaction priced from last epoch's parameters underpays its fee or its script budget and is rejected at submission.
classes.fuzz: cached parameter sets with fetch times spread across an epoch boundary, paired with live sets whose fee coefficients, min-ADA per byte and execution unit prices differ from the cached ones

classes.property: A signed body can be submitted once: every transaction this builder signs is bound to something that cannot repeat, a specific input it spends, a validity interval that closes, or a nonce carried in its datum or metadata. Resubmitting a body the builder already signed is refused before it reaches the node.
classes.fuzz: a captured signed body resubmitted inside and outside its validity interval, with its inputs still unspent and after they are spent, and with the wallet's UTxO set changed underneath it

classes.property: Coin selection runs within a bound the builder documents: for a wallet holding many small UTxOs, selection completes inside that bound on inputs considered and transaction size, or it fails with a stated reason. Anyone able to send UTxOs to the wallet decides how many it holds, so the bound is what keeps that out of their hands.
classes.fuzz: wallets of 1 to 10000 UTxOs, most of them dust carrying many token names, with the payment amount held fixed

classes.property: The script data hash in the body commits to the redeemers, datums and cost models the witness set actually carries: for any transaction with a script input, recomputing the hash over the witness set reproduces the value in the body, and removing, reordering or reindexing a redeemer changes it. A body whose hash disagrees with its witness set fails phase 1 and the scripts never run.
classes.fuzz: transactions with a redeemer removed, a redeemer's tag or index changed, a datum dropped from the witness set, and a cost model taken from another protocol version

classes.property: Collateral is capped: for any transaction with a script input, the total collateral selected stays inside the ceiling computed from the fee and the collateral percentage, and a collateral return output carries the remainder. A failing script forfeits every collateral input whole, so selection with no ceiling burns the entire UTxO it happened to pick.
classes.fuzz: wallets whose largest UTxO exceeds the required collateral by orders of magnitude, fees from the minimum to the block limit, and collateral percentages from every recent protocol parameter set

classes.property: Every transaction the builder signs pays at least the ledger minimum under the current protocol parameters: calculate the encoded transaction size with its script integrity hash and final witnesses, execution-unit fees, and the tiered reference-script fee over every reference script carried by its inputs and reference inputs. Validate the fee calculation to the lovelace against landed transactions, comparing encoded size, fee and reference scripts from Koios tx_info or an equivalent ledger source.
classes.fuzz: transactions at and one byte past size and reference-script tier boundaries, missing script-integrity-hash bytes in fee estimates, multiple reference scripts on spent and reference inputs, witness-count changes, and fees one lovelace below the recomputed minimum

classes.property: Every script purpose in the body, including spend, mint, withdrawal and certificate purposes, has the matching script in the witness set or on a reference input the body names. Phase-2 evaluation success does not establish that the actual submitted witness set is complete.
classes.fuzz: bodies with one purpose's witness removed, a zero withdrawal from a script credential, a missing observer or certificate script, a reference input without script bytes, and a script whose hash or language differs from the purpose

classes.property: Every body with any Plutus purpose carries eligible collateral inputs within the current protocol's input-count and collateral-percentage limits, with total collateral accounted for and a valid collateral return for any excess. The hosted caller must supply collateral even when script evaluation succeeds.
classes.fuzz: Plutus spend, mint and zero-withdrawal bodies with no collateral, a hosted caller omitting its settler wallet, insufficient or ineligible collateral, too many collateral inputs, and missing or invalid excess collateral returns

classes.property: Bodies produced in one builder pass spend pairwise-disjoint inputs, including fee inputs, or explicitly chain each predecessor's change into the next body and submit in dependency order. Run the batch against a mempool fake that refuses a double spend: every independent body must remain admissible after earlier bodies are accepted.
classes.fuzz: batches of one to many settlements using one settler wallet, repeated spent fee inputs, collateral reserved by another pending body, concurrent builds from the same UTxO snapshot, and chained bodies submitted both in and out of dependency order

taxonomies.note: Hosted services reading hostile provider data and sharing process resources. A tracked Python test file is test_*.py, *_test.py, or any .py under test/, tests/ or __tests__/. A pytest test function (def or async def whose name starts test_ and contains the class id) specifies a class. Files importing hypothesis are noted as properties; other matches are examples. Naming an import alone does not prove the test exercises a generator; review its assertions and bounds.

classes.property: Every provider row at an address outsiders can pay to is decoded item by item within documented byte, nesting and work bounds. A malformed or unsupported row is contained to that item and cannot crash the route or corrupt an honest row.
classes.fuzz: Byron-era outputs, reference scripts with bytes and with bytes null or absent, deep timelocks, and CBOR or JSON at and beyond each documented depth or size bound

classes.property: Mixing N stranger outputs into an honest wallet or vault never makes the honest read refuse. Unsupported outsider items are isolated while valid controlled outputs remain readable; unknown items never become trusted funds.
classes.fuzz: honest wallets and vaults with zero to many unrelated outputs interleaved in every page and order, malformed rows among valid rows, and one hostile row at each pagination boundary

classes.property: Over-long literals and over-deep nesting are refused per item within stated bounds, without failing an entire provider answer or escaping the route's controlled error handling.
classes.fuzz: JSON integer literals at and beyond CPython's conversion limit (including more than 4300 digits), huge strings, duplicate keys, and JSON and CBOR at the nesting limit and one level beyond it

classes.property: Provider requests per unauthenticated request stay within a documented bound as stranger rows grow. A process-wide budget also bounds the sustained provider rate over a documented time window across concurrent requests; a per-request cap alone is insufficient.
classes.fuzz: stranger-row and page counts at and one past each documented limit, repeated and concurrent unauthenticated requests across routes, slow providers, and retries across process-wide budget window boundaries

classes.property: No async route performs synchronous work growing with outsider input on the event loop. Probe every async route with a slow synchronous dependency and hostile row growth; independent event-loop work must remain responsive within a documented bound.
classes.fuzz: every async route with a slow synchronous provider, nested-script hashing, CBOR decoding, or cache miss; increasing outsider rows; and a concurrent heartbeat or unrelated request

classes.property: The service names and bounds its shared threadpool tokens, caches and single-writer stores such as sqlite. Flooding one route cannot exhaust resources needed by the others; unrelated routes continue serving within documented admission and latency bounds.
classes.fuzz: request floods at and past threadpool capacity, distinct script keys at and past cache capacity, sqlite writer contention, cancellations while holding resources, and simultaneous requests to unrelated routes

taxonomies.note: Compact contracts and Midnight builders require generator-backed TypeScript/JavaScript or Python tests, or a scoped waiver. Static declaration coverage does not prove runtime execution.

classes.property: Declared transcript gas fits current submission state with headroom, including populated tries; deploy-time empty-state measurements alone cannot satisfy it.
classes.fuzz: Post at least three entries sequentially and concurrently, and vary existing map depth and size.

classes.property: Concurrent inserts either both land consistently or one retries safely from current state; no accepted update is lost.
classes.fuzz: Race same-key and distinct-key inserts against growing state.

classes.property: An immutable deployment refuses every upgrade or authority replacement; a mutable control proves the tested path is reachable.
classes.fuzz: Try empty, random, substituted and committee authority modes with real signature controls.

classes.property: The verifier binds the contract address, circuit, statement, network genesis and required finality.
classes.fuzz: Swap each binding independently and vary finality proofs.

classes.property: Deployment inspection rejects swapped verifier keys, extra operations, added authority and pre-seeded state.
classes.fuzz: Mutate each deployed artifact and initial-state field independently.

classes.property: Private witness material does not escape through proof servers, logs or errors.
classes.fuzz: Generate malformed witnesses with distinctive private bytes and inspect all errors and outbound boundaries.

classes.property: Only explicitly justified public values are disclosed; private witness changes preserve the declared disclosure policy.
classes.fuzz: Vary private preimages and inspect public outputs and disclosures.

classes.property: Compiler, runtime and ledger target versions match deployment pins; incompatible versions refuse before submission.
classes.fuzz: Vary compiler/runtime and ledger version combinations around supported pins.

classes.property: A proof or transaction cannot be reused across contracts, networks or consumed nonces.
classes.fuzz: Replay captured proofs and signed transactions with altered domain, state and nonce.

taxonomies.note: Rust services and off-chain code that read hostile bytes and move value. Active when the repository tracks a Rust test function. A class is specified by a Rust test function whose name carries the class id: a function under #[test] or a sibling attribute such as #[tokio::test] or #[rstest], including the functions a proptest! block declares. A helper no test build collects, a comment and a string do not count. A match in a file that uses proptest, quickcheck, bolero, arbtest or Kani is a property over a generator; a match in a file without one is noted as an example. A crate that builds Cardano transactions owes the builder classes as well: copy them from the typescript taxonomy into this one's classes, where they are then specified by Rust tests.

classes.property: No bytes an outsider can supply make the process panic or abort: every decoder, parser and verifier returns a typed error for malformed, truncated, oversized and adversarially nested input. A panic in a service is a restart an attacker can repeat, and in a consensus or signing path it is a halt.
classes.fuzz: arbitrary byte strings and structure-aware mutations of valid inputs: truncation at every offset, length prefixes beyond the remaining input, nesting at and past the documented depth, non-canonical encodings and invalid UTF-8

classes.property: Memory reserved while decoding is bounded by the bytes actually received, never by a length the input declares: a length prefix, an element count or a capacity hint from the wire does not size an allocation before the data behind it has arrived, and the total decoded size stays under a documented cap.
classes.fuzz: inputs declaring lengths and counts from zero to u64::MAX with little or no payload behind them, deeply nested containers, and many small messages against one connection

classes.property: Arithmetic on amounts, fees, indexes and timestamps is checked in the build that ships: an operation that would overflow, underflow, divide by zero or lose value in a conversion returns an error, and no result wraps or truncates. A release build wraps by default, so the property has to hold under the release profile and not only in a debug test run.
classes.fuzz: operands at and around zero, one, and each type's MIN and MAX, values that overflow only after scaling by decimals or a rate, and conversions between every integer width the code uses

classes.property: What this code encodes it decodes to the same value, and it agrees with the other implementation of the same format: for any value, decoding its encoding yields that value, and the bytes equal the reference encoder's for the same input. Two readers of one wire format that disagree on a single input let a signer approve one thing while a verifier checks another.
classes.fuzz: values across each field's full range, canonical and non-canonical encodings of the same value, and the same vectors run through the reference implementation, with bytes and decoded values both compared

classes.property: A failure in a value-moving step stops the operation: no error from a write, a submit, a transfer or a signature check is discarded, logged and continued past, or replaced by a default. The caller of a step that failed observes the failure, and nothing that depended on the step has happened.
classes.fuzz: fault injection at every fallible call on the path: I/O errors, timeouts, partial writes, and a dependency returning each error variant it declares, with the resulting state compared against the state before the call

classes.property: Every payload this code signs is one it built, or one it decoded and checked against the request that asked for it: the inputs it spends, the outputs and amounts it intends, and no certificate, withdrawal, mint or metadata beyond them. A transaction returned by a remote resolver, a counterparty or a worker is hostile until it has been checked.
classes.fuzz: well-formed transactions that differ from the request in one field: an extra output, a redirected change address, a raised fee, an added withdrawal or mint, a swapped input, and a body for another network

classes.property: Key material and credentials never reach a log line, an error value, a panic message or a Debug or Display rendering: types that hold them do not derive Debug over the secret, and every error built on a path that touches them is free of it.
classes.fuzz: distinctive secret bytes driven through every failing path, with logs, error chains, panic output and formatted values searched for them in raw, hex and base64 forms

classes.property: The work one unauthenticated request can cause stays within a documented bound as outsider-controlled data grows: upstream calls, database rows read and bytes allocated per request are capped, and a process-wide budget bounds the sustained rate across concurrent requests. A cap per request alone is not a bound.
classes.fuzz: row, page and item counts at and one past each documented limit, repeated and concurrent unauthenticated requests across routes, slow upstreams, and retries across the budget window boundary

classes.property: No async task does blocking or CPU-bound work that grows with outsider input on a runtime worker thread: such work runs on a blocking pool or is bounded, so an unrelated task stays responsive within a documented bound while a hostile request is being served.
classes.fuzz: every async entry point with a slow synchronous dependency, hashing, decoding or a cache miss over growing outsider input, measured against a concurrent heartbeat task

classes.property: Every queue, channel, connection pool, semaphore and cache the service shares is bounded and named, and flooding one route cannot exhaust what the others need: an unbounded channel is memory an outsider controls, and a permit held across an await that never completes is a route that never serves again.
classes.fuzz: request floods at and past each capacity, distinct keys at and past cache capacity, cancellation while holding a permit or a lock, and simultaneous requests to unrelated routes

taxonomies.note: FRAME pallets and runtimes (Polkadot SDK, Cardano partner chains), after the vulnerability classes Parity publishes as the Polkadot Top Ten and the obligations FRAME itself states as attributes. Active when a tracked Rust file declares a pallet or assembles a runtime. A class is specified by a Rust test function whose name carries the class id, by the same rule as the rust taxonomy; a match in a file that uses proptest, quickcheck, bolero, arbtest or Kani is a property, and any other match is noted as an example over the cases it lists. A test named for a class shows the class was declared, never that it runs or bites: the project harness has to execute it.

classes.property: Every dispatchable's declared weight covers its worst case, proof size included: for the largest arguments the call admits and the fullest storage it can meet, measured execution stays within the declared weight. An underweight call lets one transaction fill a block for the price of a small one.
classes.fuzz: arguments at each bound the call accepts, storage populated to its declared maximum, and the declared weight compared with measured reference time and proof size on the worst-case path

classes.property: No call, hook or runtime API walks a collection whose length an account can grow without paying for each step: iteration over storage, over a vector argument or over a prefix is bounded by a constant the weight accounts for, or is paged. This holds for on_initialize, on_finalize and on_idle above all, which run whether or not anyone pays.
classes.fuzz: collections grown to and past their declared bound by many accounts, with each call and each hook measured as the count rises

classes.property: No extrinsic, inherent, hook or runtime API panics on input an account or a block author controls: indexing, slicing, division, decoding, unwrap and expect are unreachable for every admissible call. A panic in a dispatchable invalidates a transaction; a panic in a hook or an inherent stops block production.
classes.fuzz: every call with arguments at and beyond each bound, empty and maximal vectors, zero divisors and malformed SCALE bytes, and every hook run at genesis, at session and era boundaries and over empty storage

classes.property: Balances, counters, weights and indexes use checked or saturating arithmetic whose saturation is itself safe: no addition, subtraction, multiplication or conversion wraps or truncates in the runtime's release build, and a result that saturated never credits or debits the wrong amount.
classes.fuzz: operands at zero, one and each type's maximum, amounts that overflow only after scaling, repeated accumulation across blocks, and conversions between the balance, block-number and weight types

classes.property: Every byte an account can place in storage is paid for by a deposit or bounded per account: creating an entry reserves an amount proportional to its size, entries have a maximum encoded length, and removing them returns the deposit. Storage that is free to fill is a permanent cost on every node.
classes.fuzz: many accounts creating entries of minimal and maximal size, accounts with exactly the deposit and one unit less, and create-then-remove cycles with the reserved balance checked at each step

classes.property: Every dispatchable checks its origin before it reads state or changes it: a privileged call refuses a signed caller, a signed call refuses none, and no call reaches a write on an origin it did not match. The check is on the call itself, not on a caller the pallet assumes.
classes.fuzz: each call dispatched from none, from root, from every signed role the pallet distinguishes and from each custom origin, with otherwise valid arguments

classes.property: A call admitted without a signature can be included once: its validation binds it to state that changes when it executes, runs when the call enters the pool and again at dispatch, and gives it a unique provides tag and a bounded longevity. An unsigned call with no such binding can be resubmitted for as long as anyone likes, at no cost.
classes.fuzz: the same unsigned payload resubmitted in the same block, in later blocks and after the state it proves has moved on, and payloads produced for another chain, another pallet instance or another era

classes.property: Data a block author supplies as an inherent is checked by every importing node against what that node itself observes: check_inherent rejects a block whose inherent disagrees with the verifier's own source beyond a documented tolerance, and a missing required inherent is an error. An inherent nobody checks is whatever the block author says it is.
classes.fuzz: blocks carrying an inherent with altered, stale, future-dated, duplicated and missing data, imported by a node whose own source disagrees, at and beyond the tolerance

classes.property: No failure inside a dispatchable or a hook is discarded: the result of a transfer, a reserve, an unreserve, a repatriation or a nested dispatch is propagated, or handled by a fallback that is itself tested, so a call never reports success for an effect that did not happen and never leaves funds reserved that the code believes it released.
classes.fuzz: each fallible currency and dispatch call forced to fail or to succeed in part: an account with less reserved than expected, a destination that cannot exist, a balance at the existential deposit

classes.property: No outcome a caller or a block author profits from depends on a value either of them can choose or predict: randomness comes from a verifiable source used with its documented delay, never from a block hash, a timestamp, an extrinsic index or collective flip.
classes.fuzz: the same call repeated across blocks and forks with the author controlling timestamps and ordering, checking that outcomes cannot be selected by withholding or reordering

classes.property: An account's existence agrees with what depends on it: provider, consumer and sufficient references are taken and released in pairs, so no account is reaped while a pallet still holds state for it and none is kept alive for free.
classes.fuzz: accounts created, funded to exactly the existential deposit, drained and re-created while holding each kind of pallet state, with reference counts and remaining storage checked after every step

classes.property: A runtime upgrade leaves storage decodable and every invariant holding: each migration is idempotent, bounded in weight, guarded by the storage version it bumps, and its pre- and post-upgrade checks pass against state shaped like the live chain's. A migration that runs twice, or past the block limit, breaks the chain it upgrades.
classes.fuzz: state at each earlier storage version, empty and at its maximum, with the migration applied once and applied twice, and its weight measured against the block limit
